context: The title at the upper left reads “Hash table with chaining.” Two pale green panels, one above the other, show the best and worst cases for the same six key-value pairs, (k₁, s₁) through (k₆, s₆).

On the left of each panel, a pale blue column represents the bucket array. It contains the head of each nonempty bucket’s list and an ellipsis (…) for the remaining buckets. Horizontal arrows on the right link the nodes in each bucket’s singly linked list.
description: The upper panel shows the best case: the pairs are evenly distributed across buckets, and lookup takes O(1) time. The six pairs are spread evenly across the three buckets shown. The first links (k₁, s₁) → (k₂, s₂), the second (k₃, s₃) → (k₄, s₄), and the third (k₅, s₅) → (k₆, s₆). Each list is short, with just 2 nodes, so lookup takes a constant number of comparisons once the bucket is located. As the data set grows, O(1) lookup also requires a suitable load factor to keep the average chain length constant. An even distribution alone does not guarantee this bound.

The lower panel shows the worst case: all pairs land in one bucket, and lookup takes O(n) time. All six pairs map to the first bucket and form a singly linked list of 6 nodes: (k₁, s₁) → (k₂, s₂) → (k₃, s₃) → (k₄, s₄) → (k₅, s₅) → (k₆, s₆). The remaining buckets below, represented by an ellipsis, are empty. The hash table has effectively become a singly linked list. Finding its last element requires checking all n nodes.

frames.explanation: Trace a lookup for k₆. In the upper panel, locate the third bucket and check only k₅ and k₆. In the lower panel, start at k₁ and traverse the entire chain, checking all 6 entries.
frames.title: Six key-value pairs: O(1) lookup with an even distribution and O(n) with a single chain

result: The hash algorithm should spread the keys as evenly as possible. Combined with a suitable load factor, this keeps chains short and avoids concentrating all keys in one bucket.
summary: The same six key-value pairs take different numbers of comparisons to search, depending on whether they are evenly distributed or all in one bucket.
title: Best- and worst-case distributions in a hash table with chaining
